solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Wooden ship's prow heeled over

indicators.note: the prow is the front of a ship, so the first letter of the word ship's is taken

parts.note: a vessel that has heeled over is leaning, or tilted

explanation.surface: A wooden vessel's bow has keeled to one side.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Wooden' looks like part of the ship picture, but it is the definition in its sense of stiff and awkward.
explanation.definitionFit: Stiff, unnatural speech or acting is described both as wooden and as stilted: synonyms.

clue.text: Reduce time in seaside, heading north

indicators.note: in means the time letter goes inside the seaside

parts.note: the shore is the seaside

indicators.note: heading means the first letter of north

explanation.surface: Cut short a trip to the coast and make for the north.
explanation.definitionFit: To reduce the length of something is to cut it down: a synonym.

clue.text: Unbeliever died moving down centre of arena

indicators.note: moving down says the died letter shifts lower in this down entry

parts.note: an infidel is one who rejects a faith

explanation.surface: A heretic dies and is carried into the middle of an amphitheatre.
explanation.walkthrough: 'moving down' moves the D of INFIDEL two places further down the word.
explanation.definitionFit: In cricket and baseball the area nearer the middle of the ground is the infield.

clue.text: Tool often needed grabbing sugar initially

definitions.text: Tool often needed grabbing sugar initially

indicators.note: initially means take the first letter of each of the five words

explanation.surface: A utensil that is frequently required for picking up sugar lumps.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is both the wordplay and the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Small pincers called sugar tongs are the traditional implement for lifting sugar lumps.

clue.text: Run down, round, then run right

parts.note: a disc is a round object
R is the cricket abbreviation for run
to right a text is to correct, or edit, it

explanation.surface: A list of joggers' instructions: turn, then run, then turn right.
explanation.definitionFit: To run someone down is to criticise and damage their reputation: a synonym.

clue.text: Instrument producing power with final note

parts.note: force is strength or power
PS, postscript, is a note added at the end of a letter

explanation.surface: A musical instrument that delivers volume, ending on one last note.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Instrument' and 'note' suggest music, but the instrument is a surgical one and the note is a postscript.
explanation.definitionFit: Surgeons use a pair of pincers called forceps, an example of a medical instrument.

clue.text: Control for audio device editing recording originally

indicators.note: originally means take the opening letter of each of the five words

explanation.surface: A sound-desk knob used to edit a recording.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Control for audio device' looks like the whole definition, but only 'Control' is.
explanation.definitionFit: A sliding knob on a mixing desk that adjusts sound level is a fader: a type of control.

clue.text: Change ends in intimate apparel getting forward

indicators.note: change ends in means swap the first and last letters of the intimate word

parts.note: a dear is a close, beloved person
a dress is an item of apparel

explanation.surface: A lingerie shopper alters the hems and gets bolder.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Change ends in' swaps the D and R of DEAR to give READ.
explanation.definitionFit: Mail sent on to a new address is forwarded, which means it has a new address written on it.

clue.text: Cheer two-thirds of team getting knocked back

indicators.note: two-thirds of means only the first four of the six letters are kept

parts.note: a football or cricket side has eleven players, so is called an eleven
to knock back food or drink is to consume it, so ate

explanation.surface: A side reduced by a third is pushed back but still cheers.
explanation.definitionFit: To cheer someone is to lift their spirits, which is to raise or uplift them: a synonym.

clue.text: Doubt party accepts American president's inauguration

indicators.note: accepts means the party takes the other pieces in

parts.note: a sect is a faction or party

indicators.note: an inauguration is a beginning, so the first letter of president's

explanation.surface: A faction allows in a US leader's swearing-in, with misgivings.
explanation.definitionFit: To doubt someone's honesty is to mistrust or be wary of them: a synonym.

clue.text: Puts out 'top and tails'

definitions.meaning: read as OFF (to top, slang for kill) plus ENDS (tails)

explanation.walkthrough: To 'top' is British slang for to kill, i.e. to off; tails are ends. The quotation marks invite reading the phrase as two words.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who puts others out upsets or annoys them, which is what one does who offends.

clue.text: Son embarrassed over purchasing new pants

indicators.note: purchasing here means taking in or holding, so one piece goes inside the other
over tells us the pair son-plus-embarrassed is read backwards

parts.note: an embarrassed person goes red
raw means new or inexperienced, as a raw recruit

explanation.surface: A young man blushes while buying some fresh underwear.
explanation.walkthrough: 'over' reverses son-plus-embarrassed to DERS; 'purchasing' is not buying here but holding the new piece inside.
explanation.definitionFit: Pants in British English means underpants, and old-fashioned knickers are called drawers: synonyms.

clue.text: Chamberlain, perhaps, empty talker clutching half-hearted comfort

indicators.note: clutching means holding, so the comforting word sits inside
an empty word keeps only its outside letters, here those of talker
half-hearted means one of the two central letters of the word is lost

parts.note: to reassure someone is to comfort them

explanation.surface: A wind-bag is clinging to some lukewarm consolation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'half-hearted' removes one of the two middle S's of REASSURE, leaving REASURE. A chamberlain is historically the officer who manages a household's or city's finances.
explanation.definitionFit: A chamberlain, as in the Chamberlain of the City of London, is an officer in charge of funds: an example.

clue.text: Bird's day with ladies' man

parts.note: a rake is a dissolute womaniser

explanation.surface: A woman spends a day out with a smooth charmer, 'bird' being British slang for a girlfriend.
explanation.definitionFit: A male duck is called a drake, an example of a bird.

clue.text: Naturists closed unit backing trousers

indicators.note: backing means the concealed letters run in reverse order
trousers used as a verb means pockets, so the words hold the answer inside them

explanation.surface: Nudists in a members-only group are putting their weight behind wearing trousers, of all things.
explanation.walkthrough: 'trousers' is a verb: the words closed unit pocket SEDUN, which 'backing' reverses.
explanation.definitionFit: Naturists go about unclothed, and people without clothes are nudes: a loose synonym.

clue.text: Nearly unclothed dash consumed by endless 'Drink, drink!'

indicators.note: consumed by means swallowed inside the other piece
endless means the last letter is removed

parts.note: the drink is slang for the sea

indicators.note: nearly means the last letter is dropped

parts.note: unclothed is naked
a dash is a small amount, a bit

explanation.surface: A half-naked dash is swallowed by a frantic call for alcohol.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Drink, drink!' looks like one shout: the first is the sea ('the drink'), cut to SE by 'endless'. Snakebite is a British pub drink of lager and cider.
explanation.definitionFit: A mix of cider and lager known in British pubs is a snakebite, an example of a drink.

clue.text: Separate hollow covers providing iron earth's core

indicators.note: covers means the hollow goes round the other pieces

parts.note: a dent is a hollow in a surface
providing means if, as in 'providing it rains'
Fe is the chemical symbol for iron

indicators.note: the core of a word is its middle letter, here of earth

explanation.surface: A distinct hollow conceals an iron-rich centre of the earth.
explanation.walkthrough: The middle of the five-letter EARTH is R.
explanation.definitionFit: Separate, as in 'two separate issues', means distinct, i.e. not the same.

clue.text: Planning scrap, boxing over interval, cut

indicators.note: boxing means enclosing the other pieces

parts.note: a scrap is a fight
O is the cricket abbreviation for over

indicators.note: cut means the last letter is chopped off

parts.note: a rest is a pause or interval

explanation.surface: A boxing bout is shortened after an interval between rounds.
explanation.walkthrough: 'boxing' and 'interval' suggest a prize fight, but 'boxing' signals enclosing.
explanation.definitionFit: Foresight is thought taken in advance for the future, a synonym for planning.

clue.text: Spot healed around spot for treatment

indicators.note: around means the healed word wraps round the resort

parts.note: someone healed is better
a spa is a place for health treatment

explanation.surface: A spot heals over at a clinic where it is being treated.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Spot' at the start is the verb, to splash; 'spot' later is a place.
explanation.definitionFit: To spot with dirt is to speckle or splash it, which is to bespatter.

clue.text: British leader's useless in providing amusement

indicators.note: in means the useless letters go inside

parts.note: a king is a leader
US, short for unserviceable, means useless

explanation.surface: A British monarch who is no good is merely being entertaining.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's is 'is'. US for useless is a slang abbreviation for unserviceable.
explanation.definitionFit: Street performers busk, entertaining passers-by for money, so the definition works loosely.

clue.text: Hunted rabbit constrained by speed, occasionally

indicators.note: constrained by means held within the other letters
occasionally means take alternate letters of speed

parts.note: rabbit is rhyming slang (rabbit and pork) for talk

explanation.surface: A rabbit is caught by a fast runner every so often.
explanation.walkthrough: Rabbit is Cockney rhyming slang: rabbit and pork, talk. The rabbit is not the quarry.
explanation.definitionFit: To stalk prey is to hunt it stealthily, so stalked is a past tense of that.

clue.text: Inspects container ship's exterior

indicators.note: exterior means the ship letters lie outside the container

parts.note: SS, steamship, is the standard abbreviation before a ship's name
a can is a container

explanation.surface: An inspector checks the hull of a container vessel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'container ship' looks like a single phrase, but the two words do separate jobs.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who scans a page or a crowd examines it: a synonym of inspects.

clue.text: Shellfish and sole beneath sailor on sea finally

indicators.note: on means placed after, in this down entry below
beneath means the next piece comes below in this down entry

parts.note: AB, able seaman, is a sailor

indicators.note: finally means the last letter of sea

parts.note: sole means single, alone, lone

explanation.surface: Shellfish and sole served to a sailor on the sea.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sole' is a fish in the surface, but means lone.
explanation.definitionFit: An abalone is an edible sea snail prized for its shell: a shellfish.

clue.text: Delight, for example, holding fine model up

indicators.note: holding means taking the other letters within

parts.note: say means for example

indicators.note: up in a down clue means the letters read upwards, backwards

parts.note: F is the abbreviation for fine, as on pencils
to sit for an artist is to model

explanation.surface: Delight, for instance, keeping a stylish catwalk model on high.
explanation.definitionFit: To satisfy someone is to please or gratify them, a synonym for delight.

clue.text: Source of gas market includes hydrogen

indicators.note: includes means the hydrogen letter goes inside

parts.note: a sale is a market event, a selling
H is the chemical symbol for hydrogen

explanation.surface: The gas market includes hydrogen as a fuel.
explanation.definitionFit: Fracking extracts natural gas from sedimentary rock of this kind, so it is a gas source.

clue.text: Gripped by desires, is tantalisingly unyielding

indicators.note: gripped by says the answer is held within the following words

explanation.surface: Someone tantalisingly held in the grip of yearning still stands firm.
explanation.definitionFit: Something unyielding will not give way, and is therefore able to withstand: a synonym.

clue.text: Teases about sweetheart's tantrums

indicators.note: about means the teasing word goes around

parts.note: to rag someone is to tease them
the heart of sweet is its middle letter, E

explanation.surface: Someone mocks their partner's outbursts.
explanation.definitionFit: Fits of anger and tantrums are both rages: synonyms.

clue.text: Sadly upset describing end of morris dance

indicators.note: describing here means drawing round, encircling
upset in a down clue means turned over, read upwards

parts.note: alas is a cry of sadness

indicators.note: end of means the last letter of morris

explanation.surface: Morris dancers sadly abandon their dance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upset' turns ALAS to SALA; 'describing' puts it round the S. Morris dancing is a traditional English folk dance.
explanation.definitionFit: Salsa is a lively Latin American dance.

clue.text: Suspicion of stink lingering about

indicators.note: about means around, so the letters lie within the words stink lingering

explanation.surface: Someone suspects a bad smell is hanging around.
explanation.definitionFit: A faint suspicion or hint of something is an inkling: synonyms.

clue.text: Bestial sounds by criminal circling scaffold

indicators.note: by means next to, joining the two pieces
circling means turning the criminal word right round

parts.note: a lag is a convict, especially an old lag
cattle low, so lows are animal noises

explanation.surface: Animals bellow as a felon is led around the place of execution.
explanation.definitionFit: The scaffold is the platform for executions, and the gallows is the frame for hanging: synonyms.

clue.text: Judgement's not done accepting singular deity

indicators.note: accepting means taking in the other piece
not done is non-U, socially unacceptable, so the U is removed

parts.note: a guess is a judgement or estimate; the 's is 'is'
singular can mean odd, peculiar

explanation.surface: A verdict is still pending, but it takes in one particular god.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not done' means non-U (U = upper-class, acceptable), so 'not done' removes the U, leaving GESS.
explanation.definitionFit: A female god is a goddess, so the word is a type of deity.

clue.text: King Lear possibly turned grey, overcome by stress

indicators.note: overcome by means surrounded by the stress word

parts.note: to try is to strain or put under stress
someone who has turned grey has aged

explanation.surface: The old king's hair whitened under the strain.
explanation.walkthrough: Shakespeare's King Lear ages and suffers under strain, so the surface fits the definition too.
explanation.definitionFit: King Lear is one of Shakespeare's great tragic plays: an example of the genre.
